title: Dream owners decry midday Finals Game 6 after scheduling chaos: 'Earned the right to be taken seriously' - CBS Sports
description: The Dream's must-win WNBA Finals game was rescheduled to 12:30 p.m. on Thursday
body:
The Dream's must-win WNBA Finals game was rescheduled to 12:30 p.m. on Thursday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Atlanta Dream ownership group wrote an open letter to the city of Atlanta and the team's fans Tuesday regarding the decision to play Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals -- now a must-win for the Dream -- at 12:30 p.m. ET on Thursday. In the letter, the ownership group claimed that it raised concerns about potential scheduling conflicts at State Farm Arena months ago that "did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved." Additionally, the letter noted that "playing a midday game on a Thursday is not what we would have chosen and not what we fought for."The Dream's primary home, Gateway Center Arena, is the smallest arena in the league, with a capacity of just 3,500. That is not ideal for any playoff game, but especially not a Finals game, and the Dream have played all five of their postseason contests at State Farm Arena -- the 17,000-seat arena that is home to the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. 
        
            
                WNBA Finals Game 6 moved to early afternoon with Dream to host Valkyries at State Farm Arena
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Due to scheduling conflicts, including a Sombr concert and a Hawks game, Games 3 and 4 of the Finals had to be altered so they could take place at State Farm Arena. Game 3 was moved from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21, while Game 4 was moved up to 1 p.m. ET in order to accommodate a doubleheader with the Hawks' matchup against the Houston Rockets, which was moved back to 8 p.m. 
The Hawks are also scheduled to play at home on both Wednesday and Thursday this week, causing another conflict with Game 6. Faced with no good options, the league eventually chose to play Game 6 in the afternoon in order to ensure it was played at the much larger State Farm Arena. Here is the full letter from the Dream's ownership group:Dear Atlanta Dream Fans,First, thank you. Thank you for showing up, showing out, and supporting the Atlanta Dream. Thank you for your patience, your flexibility, and your willingness to navigate all the hurdles being placed in front of us. This postseason has asked a lot of our fans, our partners, our players, and our city.But ATL knows how to handle adversity.  It's what we do.  And once again, the city and our fans will fill the building.  On a workday. On a school day.  In the early afternoon.  We do not take that support for granted.This incredible run by our players has also made something else abundantly clear: the Atlanta Dream has earned the right to be taken seriously.Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena.  As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns.  Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved.Perhaps it was assumed that the Dream would not make it this far. Perhaps, our place in the Finals was not accounted for.  Whatever the reason, the reality is that we are here. We earned our place in the Finals, and our city deserves the opportunity to show up for its team.Playing a midday game on a Thursday is not what we would have chosen and not what we fought for.  And as much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage. That meant State Farm Arena.  We are grateful to everyone who helped make that possible, especially our partners - the Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena - who stepped up by adjusting their schedule on the fly, not once, but three times. And what a celebration it has been: a party, a concert and incredible Dream basketball all rolled into one.That is what Atlanta supporting Atlanta looks like.The Hawks and the Dream are different teams with different histories, but we share a city, a community, and a responsibility to help Atlanta shine on the biggest stages. When one of us has an opportunity to make history, we all want to see it happen.We have built something special here, powered by our players, our fans, our partners, and a city that believes in what we are doing.  We intend to keep building. We intend to keep winning.  And we expect the opportunities, planning, and consideration afforded to us to reflect the level at which we compete.  We are proud to represent Atlanta. We are proud to be in the Finals. And we are grateful for the way this city has rallied around us.Thank you,Atlanta Dream Ownership – Larry, Robyn, Suzanne & ReneeThe decision to hold a Finals decider at lunchtime in Atlanta, and early in the morning in San Francisco, has received significant criticism, including from CBS Sports' Lindsay Gibbs. 

        
            
                WNBA Finals' Game 6 scheduling debacle is an embarrassing end to a historic season
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
And, because the arena will need to be cleared quickly to change it over for the Hawks' game against the Cleveland Cavaliers, which has been pushed back to 8 p.m. ET, there could be major logistical challenges if the Valkyries win and clinch their first-ever championship. Most notably, if the Valkyries win the title, their celebration may not happen on the court, as is tradition, but would be moved to a practice gym, according to ESPN.

title: NWSL Team of the Week: Croix Bethune breaks single-season assists record; Denver duo shines - CBS Sports
description: Plenty of players deserved a spot, but here are the ones who stood out most

Plenty of players deserved a spot, but here are the ones who stood out most

        No more second chances in the 2026 NWSL regular season. Decision Day is upon us, and before the chaos kicks off, players across the league are setting pitches ablaze with crucial performances. That means it's time to give out Attacking Third Team of the Week honors.After weekly matches across the 2026 NWSL season, Attacking Third analysts will select players, a head coach, and an honorary captain based on weekend performances. Here you can find a mix of stats and data, analysis from our pundits, and highlights you may have missed over the weekend. If you're keeping track of who earned past honors, check out our previous team of the week.It's been a wild year, and it feels like it's just getting started now that the postseason is rapidly approaching. That also means our team of the week honors will look slightly different following games moving forward. We'll hand out one more set of honors after Decision Day on November 1, but afterward, we'll be locked into playoffs and performances from the quarterfinals onward. Here's who made the latest edition:Goalkeeper: Ann-Katrin Berger (Gotham FC)When it comes to the NWSL Shield, Gotham FC is taking the long road. If they manage to lift it, it'll be because they have a great goalkeeper to keep away any spoilers. Ann-Katrin Berger is back on the team of the week honors for keeping a newly eliminated and motivated Orlando Pride from deterring Gotham's quest for the title. She faced 19 shots, eight attempts on target, and made seven saves in a narrow but crucial victory. 
Defender: Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC)Angel City's Evelyn Shores has become a bona fide two-way player this season and stands out on a backline that has Sarah Gorden and Savy King. She's back on the team of the week for another stellar performance, where she was instrumental in building up play and keeping the backline in shape. She led defenders on the team in duels (seven) and co-led in clearances (two) and interceptions (two). Defender: Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC)Not that Tierna Davidson needed any more bullet points on her long resume for NWSL defender of the year, but scoring headers in the box was already on there. She did it again for Gotham FC and scored a decisive game-winner to keep the club ahead in the NWSL Shield race
Defender: Kaleigh Kurtz (Denver Summit)If you've ever heard of the iron woman concept in NWSL, then you're already familiar with Kaleigh Kurtz, but you might not be familiar with her dance moves. She showed them off after scoring her first goal with Denver Summit.
Defender: Janine Sonis (Denver Summit)Back on the team of the week is Janine Sonis after a two-assist performance for Denver Summit in a must-win game. Denver's playoff destiny is tricky, but possible, and Sonis is making sure she's leaving with something, her seventh and eighth assists of the year.
Midfielder: Jessie Fleming (Portland Thorns)When the going gets tough this season, the tough runs away in fear of Jessie Fleming. The defensive midfielder has stepped up the club in a massive way between roster injuries and a red card suspension for Sophia Wilson. The Canadian international co-led the team in touches (66), led the team in recoveries (eight), and was a frequent outlet in building up play in a massive win over North Carolina.Midfielder: Alba Caño (Boston Legacy)Boston Legacy midfielder Alba Caño helped keep the team's spoiler reputation alive with an equalizer against San Diego. No NWSL Shield claimed on Boston's watch.
Midfielder: Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current)In 2024, Croix Bethune matched a single-season assist record (10) as a rookie. Now, it solely belongs to her. She delivered the record-setting assist to Vanessa DiBernardo for the game-winner.
Forward: Natasha Flint (Denver Summit)Seems like three points are easy to nab when Natasha Flint scores a break. The three points and goal differential could prove big in the playoff push.
Forward: Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC)Flexing her versatility over the weekend was Gisele Thompson for Angel City. Took her time on the ball and nailed the clinical finish.
Forward: Marie Muller (Portland Thorns FC)Portland Thorns are a club with a lot of history, and Marie Muller etched her name into the chapter of big moments. A lethal blast on goal clinched a playoff spot for the team.
Coach: Leif Gunnar Smerud (Angel City FC)The head-coaching rumor mill has gone pretty silent after Angel City's impressive second-half run under interim manager Leif Smerud. Another three points at home and the club is back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023. The performance is going to make it difficult for the front office to move on from the interim magician. Honorary captain: Portland's dream-making goalIt wasn't just Portland Thorns thanking Marie Muller for her game-winning goal, but several others. Not quite decision day, but it was a defining goal for several clubs. The game-winner clinched playoff spots for Portland, Kansas City Current, Utah Royals, and Angel City FC.

title: DeForest Buckner trade: Colts send DT back to 49ers in exchange for 2027 fourth-round pick - CBS Sports
description: Buckner began his NFL career with the Niners as a first round pick in 2016

Buckner began his NFL career with the Niners as a first round pick in 2016
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Indianapolis Colts announced they are trading defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, according to ESPN. Buckner will now reunite with the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.Buckner played for the Niners through the 2019 season, before joining the Colts ahead of the 2020 season. The three-time Pro Bowler will now head back to Levi's Stadium to help the Niners' defensive line.This season, he has 31 combined tackles, four sacks and three pass breakups. The 32-year-old has 683 combined tackles, including 101 for a loss, 75.5 sacks, 31 pass deflections, nine forced fumbles, 11 fumble recoveries, nine forced fumbles and two touchdowns in his 11-year career. Of the 158 games he's played in, he's started 153, including all seven so far this year. 49ers star tight end George Kittle celebrated the news on social media:
Buckner joins a defense with DT Osa Odighizuwa, DE Mykel Williams, LB Fred Warner and DE Nick Bosa, who has missed multiple games with a calf injury. The Niners defense has allowed 299.3 total yards per game, fourth-best in the league. Their run defense is their strongest area, with just 89.0 yards allowed per game, fifth-best in the league and their three rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for best.The Colts currently sit at 2-5 and second in the AFC South. They fired their general manager, Chris Ballard, and, with the changes, rumors surfaced that they would be part of a major trade as they turn to new management.It was a busy day for Indy as it also dealt Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks. With the two big moves on Tuesday, the Colts added three draft picks (two in 2027 and one in 2028) and cleared over $17.7 million in salary cap space. Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs are two more Colts players who could be involved in a trade soon.
The 49ers are in a much different spot than what Buckner is coming from at 6-1 and in first place in the NFC West. Their next game is against the Las Vegas Raiders, who are currently on a four-game losing streak, on Nov. 8.

title: Anthony Edwards injury: LaMelo Ball must level up, but there's another key - CBS Sports
description: Edwards needs surgery on his knee and is set to miss up to two months
body:
Edwards needs surgery on his knee and is set to miss up to two months
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Minnesota Timberwolves superstar Anthony Edwards is expected to miss up to two months as he undergoes arthroscopic surgery on his ailing right knee, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. This is stunning news, as it comes less than 24 hours after Edwards played like a superhero, scoring 47 points in an overtime loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday. Rather than have Edwards continue to play on the injured knee, the team decided to address the issue early in the season, with December as the target for Edwards' return, per The Athletic. The surgery is scheduled for Thursday, per ESPN. This is the same knee that gave Edwards trouble last season and he was listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Golden State Warriors with "right knee injury maintenance" earlier Tuesday. He has since been downgraded to out. Edwards, who was seen grabbing at his right knee during Sunday's win over the Toronto Raptors, missed the final game of Minnesota's first-round playoff win over the Denver Nuggets last year with a hyperextension to this same knee, but was able to return against the San Antonio Spurs for Game 1 of the conference semifinals off the bench. 
This was from The Athletic's game story on Monday night:"Edwards dealt with a hyperextended left knee in the playoffs last season and was also bothered by inflammation in his right knee. He played through it in inspiring fashion, getting around-the-clock treatment and having his right knee drained multiple times to stay available, and said in the preseason that he took most of two months off to allow both knees to heal."It sure looked like that time he took off this summer had worked. The Wolves are 3-1 and were looking like one of the league's best teams behind the electric duo of Edwards and LaMelo Ball, who was acquired from the Charlotte Hornets in a June blockbuster. Through the first week and change, Edwards is averaging 33.3 points per game and leading the league with 18 3-pointers at a 40% clip. He already has games of 45 and 47 points, and did so on a right knee that needs surgery. It's LaMelo Ball timeThe Wolves have to hold the fort down as best they can without Edwards, and their best chance at doing so in a deep Western Conference is for Ball to lead the offensive charge. Edwards is a two-way star. This will affect the Wolves' second-ranked defense, but there is more infrastructure in place on that side. Ball is Minnesota's best bet to continue creating quality offense and you'd have to imagine his scoring will tick up. Take the tiny sample for what it's worth, but so far this season the Wolves are operating at what would be a bottom-10 offensive rate over 74 non-garbage-time possessions with Ball on the court without Edwards, per Cleaning the Glass. That will obviously need to improve. 
Ball averaged over 20 points per game last year with the Hornets but is down to 14.8 this year. That's because Edwards has been so dominant, and Ball has been effective beyond his box scores by creating pace and energy. But now the Wolves need him to be more aggressive as a scorer (hopefully with some modicum of efficiency) and to prove he's ready to fully lead a team with real expectations. That said, he doesn't have to do it alone. This is where it really hurts that Donte DiVincenzo is rehabbing a torn Achilles, but the Wolves still have a handful of guys who can add to the collective effort of at least somewhat replacing Edwards' production in the aggregate. Terrence Shannon Jr. has been sensational to start the year. Jonathan Kuminga, who can create his own offense, has a real opportunity to put himself in his best light as he remains in search of the lucrative long-term contract that has eluded him. Ayo Dosunmu is a double-digit scorer and 3-point marksman who can level up. 
But none of these guys can do what the Wolves' new No. 2 can. Jaden McDaniels ready for All-Star leapMcDaniels is currently on a five-year, $136 million contract and the Wolves just signed him to a one-year, $40 million extension to set as his base number for another potential extension in 2028. In other words, McDaniels makes All-Star money and could be on his way to more than that, and he's worth it. Now he's going to have to really be worth it. McDaniels has All-Star upside, and with what should be a meaningful usage bump in Edwards' absence, this is his time to take the leap. He's averaging 15 points per game on 59% shooting so far. He's making 42% of his 3s. We know he's a demon defender, but he's been on a steady rise as a major offensive weapon who can create for himself (he has one of the best deceleration steps in the league). 
As we saw during his time with Charlotte, Ball lifts the shooting of those around him as much as any player in the league. We've already seen that in Minnesota, too, and now that McDaniels is going to be even more of a target for Ball, he could easily jump north of 20 points per game and threaten for an All-Star spot. 
Remember, this is a guy who went for 32 points and 10 boards to close out the Nuggets in Game 6 of their first-round series last year without Edwards, who was sidelined because of the same knee on which he's now set for surgery. McDaniels is a championship No. 3 option in the OG Anunoby mold, but he can be a legit No. 2 option for a "hold down the fort" stretch. It's time for him to prove it. In Ball's case, ramping up to All-Star production is the expectation. He's been at that level before. But McDaniels joining him on that level is the key to Minnesota surviving Ant's absence. The schedule at least looks friendlyBetween now and Christmas, the Wolves have only six games against upper-echelon teams: the Spurs, Rockets, Knicks, Thunder, and the Lakers (twice). 
They lose all margin for error against the Portlands and Memphis' of the league, but all things considered, this is a relatively soft stretch of schedule with 16 of their next 26 at home. title: Alabama dismisses DB Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. after second arrest - CBS Sports
description: The Crimson Tide parted ways with the defensive back after he was charged with doxing and harassing communication
body:
The Crimson Tide parted ways with the defensive back after he was charged with doxing and harassing communications toward an officer who arrested him last year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Alabama defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. was dismissed from the program after a second arrest last week, according to Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer. Kirkpatrick was arrested on Friday for allegedly threatening a police officer involved with a previous arrest online. "After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program," DeBoer said in a statement. "He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players." Kirkpatrick allegedly sent threatening messages to a University of Alabama police officer who arrested him last year, according to WBRC. He also allegedly posted a picture of the police officer and his family on his Facebook page with the caption "Dis him?" On Friday, he was charged with misdemeanor charges of doxing and harassing communications, according to multiple reports. He was initially arrested in Tuscaloosa last year on three counts of reckless endangerment, attempting to elude and speeding. Kirkpatrick was suspended for the rest of the 2025 season, but returned to the team in the spring. The defensive back also has a separate misdemeanor charge for leaving the scene of an accident last June. 
A third-year defensive back, Kirkpatrick is the son of former Alabama All-American cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick Sr. The younger Kirkpatrick served as a key reserve in the secondary, participating in 28 games over the last three years with 17 tackles.

        On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts made two major moves towards a rebuild with the trades of offensive guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Nelson's trade came first, with Indy sending him to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks for a third-round pick and a future fifth-round pick.Their second big news of the day was Indianapolis trading Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, according to ESPN. Buckner will now have a second stint with the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.These Colts trades come just about a week after firing general manager Chris Ballard. Sitting at 2-4 at the time of the firing, and 2-5 now, Indy is clearly beginning their much-needed rebuild and making those big changes along with it. 
        
            
                Quenton Nelson trade grades: Seahawks add eight-time Pro Bowler, while Colts look to sell pieces
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Niners are the opposite of a rebuild, with sights set on the playoffs and beyond. They now added a reliable defensive big man who can help get them there.
Both sides can take many positives from the deal, with the edge going to the Niners. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Colts: B+The Colts situation, sitting at 2-5, firing their GM and needing to rebuild, certainly doesn't earn a B+, but this trade does. Freeing up cap space and getting the most value for their players while they can is a smart move on their part.If the Colts kept Buckner and he signed with another team this offseason, the highest compensatory draft pick they could've received for him was a fifth-rounder. The 11-year veteran was likely going elsewhere at the end of the year anyway, emphasizing recently that at this stage in his career he wants to play winning football. 
After their loss to the Tennessee Titans, who went into the contest without a win, in Week 6, Buckner said he was "frustrated" and added, "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year." He now gets to play meaningful football, and the Colts get the most value in return. Instead of a 2028 fifth-round pick, they now have a 2027 fourth-round pick. Tuesday's moves have cleared over $17.7 million in salary cap space and added three draft picks. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    49ers: AThe 49ers' time to win is now, which means all chips are in. The Niners are one of the NFC's and the NFL's best teams at 6-1. Despite an abundance of injuries, they've managed to put on solid performances.Adding some security on the defensive line gives the team that added assurance, along with a veteran presence, someone with postseason experience and someone they know. Defensive tackles C.J. West and Alfred Collins are on IR, so the Niners were already in the market to cushion that position. Buckner has already spent multiple seasons with the team, so he not only knows the front office and schemes and has played with some of these guys before, but he will also have that extra fire that comes from a reunion with a former team.

The specifics of the plea deal and which charges he will enter a guilty plea for are not known at this time. Beasley was indicted on June 29 for allegedly manipulating his own statistics in multiple games during the 2023-24 season to allow bettors to win on prop bets. According to the indictment, Beasley worked out the scheme alongside former NBA player Ed Davis and four other named co-conspirators as part of an effort to pay off millions of dollars in gambling debts. Prosecutors were able to obtain text messages from the other defendants celebrating when Beasley shoved a teammate out of the way to go over his rebounding prop with 1.1 seconds left in a March 10 game against the Los Angeles Clippers. The scheme fell apart when Beasley went over his rebounding prop in a March 21 game against the Brooklyn Nets, causing the co-defendants to demand Davis refund their money.

"It is not evidence and Malik maintains his presumption of innocence throughout this two-year investigation. We ask that people reserve judgment until all the facts are known."
In reaching a plea deal, he becomes the second NBA player to do so after Jontay Porter pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud in 2025 for his role in a similar gambling ring. Terry Rozier also faces multiple charges in an unrelated gambling ring and has pleaded not guilty. Chauncey Billups and Damon Jones have been arrested as well in relation to an illegal poker ring, with Jones also facing illegal sports betting charges.

        The Charlotte Hornets will retire the No. 1 jersey of Muggsy Bogues on Feb. 11, the team announced Tuesday. Bogues, at 5-foot-3, is the shortest player in NBA history, and now that the Hornets will hang his jersey in the rafters of the Spectrum Center, he will become, by a wide margin, the shortest player in NBA history to have his jersey retired. That distinction was previously held by Calvin Murphy, the 5-foot-9 point guard who played his entire career for the San Diego and later Houston Rockets.Bogues, a college star at Wake Forest, was drafted No. 12 overall by the Washington Bullets in 1987. That allowed him to start his career playing next to the 7-foot-7 Manute Bol, who, at the time, was the tallest player in NBA history (a title he now shares with Gheorghe Mureșan). However, the Bullets left Bogues unprotected in the 1988 expansion draft, which allowed the incoming Charlotte Hornets to swipe him before their inaugural season.
Washington's loss was Charlotte's gain. Bogues grew into the full-time starting point guard for the Hornets during the 1989-90 season and held his post through 1997. He never made an All-Star Team or averaged more than 11.1 points per game, but he averaged double-digit assists on multiple occasions and is Charlotte's all-time leader in steals. The 90s represent the most successful era in Hornets history, with Bogues, Larry Johnson and Alonzo Mourning leading Charlotte to several postseason trips.Now, aside from his distinction as the NBA's shortest player ever, Bogues is remembered fondly for his role in Space Jam. He was one of the five then-active NBA players whose talent was stolen by the MonStars to face Michael Jordan and the Looney Tunes. 
Bogues will become the third member of the Hornets to have his jersey retired, joining former teammates Bobby Phills, who died in a car accident in 2000, and Dell Curry, who remains with the team as a broadcaster.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline targets: Ranking top players who could be traded - CBS Sports
description: Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
body:
Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL trade deadline is exactly two weeks away. That means the hot stove will heat up considerably fairly soon. We've already seen multiple high-profile deals this season, with Joey Porter Jr. heading to the Cowboys, Marvin Harrison Jr. heading to the Texans and Quenton Nelson heading to the Seahawks, and we could see several more over the next 14 days, given how wide open the league appears to be at the moment. With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at some of the top targets who could be on the move. We ranked the top 10 situations that bear the most watching, but with a twist. Some of them are team-wide, meaning there are multiple targets that interested teams could pursue over the next two weeks. There are 25 targets in all.So without further ado, here's the list...The Eagles 
Saquon Barkley's contract, with all the various option bonuses included, makes dealing with him somewhat financially complicated, but given the Eagles' struggles, his age, and the fact that teams are looking for explosiveness at running back these days, he makes sense as a target for needy teams. His current injury situation muddies the picture a bit, but that could be cleared up in the coming days and weeks as he gets further away from the hamstring pull.Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract. The Eagles just paid big money to two defensive tackles (Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis), so they probably can't afford to keep Ojomo around. He's 25 years old and has shown production upside with 6 sacks last season.  
If the Eagles want to get aggressive, they can consider dealing both him and Nolan Smith, whose fifth-year option they picked up for next season but who they probably can't afford to keep in the longer term. Smith is more of a force in the run game than as a pass rusher, but that could still be valuable for teams that need help on the edge. Dallas Goedert, meanwhile, signed a renegotiated contract with the Eagles this past offseason and is carrying only a $1.3 million base salary. He's not the most dynamic tight end these days, but he's a reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and any team that needs an additional tight end (teams love multi-tight end sets these days) could get interested for a small price. The Colts 
Nelson is already on the move, traded to the Seahawks for a pair of draft picks. Jonathan Taylor is one of the best running backs in the NFL and has been able to remain productive even while the Colts' offense has fallen apart around him. (He's only at 4.2 yards per carry, but he's carrying a 55% rushing success rate, per Pro-Football-Reference.) He's the type of explosive back who can change an offense in the way Kenneth Walker III did for the Chiefs. The contract isn't prohibitive for trade purposes, as the Colts would incur only $10 million in dead money next year if they move him. DeForest Buckner has also been traded away. 
The Titans 
It would be pretty surprising if Jeffery Simmons were dealt away, considering he recently signed a three-year, $105.8 million contract extension that made him the highest-paid defensive tackle in the NFL. But the Titans are going nowhere fast, and Simmons is by far their best asset if they want to kick-start yet another rebuild, which seems to be in the offing. Tennessee would take on a bunch of dead money by dealing him, but it might be worth it if they can get as much draft capital as he's worth. Amani Hooker is a very good, very versatile safety (he's played 232 snaps in the box, 127 as a deep safety and 56 as a slot corner so far this year), and those are valuable around the NFL. He still has three years left on his contract, including 2026, so there is a team-control aspect that would be valuable to a potentially acquiring team.  Tony Pollard is in the final year of his deal with only a $6.7 million base salary. He's 29 years old, but if you look under the hood, the numbers show he's actually running pretty well so far this season. He's 10th in yards after contact per attempt among the 39 running backs with 50-plus carries, for example, according to Tru Media. He's also 12th in explosive run rate. He can still play, and help a team in need of a committee back. 
Calvin Ridley has completely fallen out of favor in Tennessee and could potentially help a team in need of depth-chart wide receiver help. The Chargers 
Khalil Mack is on a one-year deal with an $8 million base salary. He's got three sacks in six games and has played 71% of the Chargers' defensive snaps. He's not going to be the player he once was, but any team in need of a rotational pass rusher should give the Chargers a call to see if they can get him for a late pick. Tuli Tuipulotu only has two sacks in the Chargers' six games, but a deeper look at the numbers reveals a player playing better than that. He's 23rd in pressure rate among 148 players with 100 or more pass-rush snaps, according to Tru Media, and 18th in havoc play rate. He's still just 24 years old and you can get out ahead of his free agency by acquiring him now. 
Derwin James, like Jeffery Simmons, recently signed a contract extension, so it would be somewhat surprising to see him get dealt. But he's 31 years old, the Chargers are terrible, and he's one of their most valuable assets. His base salaries for the next three years are also pretty high ($17.5 million, $24.6 million and $21.5 million), so the return might not be as much as the Chargers would be looking for. Johnston only has 8 catches for 165 scoreless yards this season, and he's seemingly been surpassed in the target pecking order. He also has an $18 million salary for next season after the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option. So the return is likely to be low, but it's hard to imagine that L.A. wants to keep him around. The Cardinals 
Budda Baker has base salaries of $14.4 million and $16.1 million this year and next, but he's a valuable enough player to make those price tags worth it. He's extremely versatile and can play both the run and the pass, whether lined up deep or in the box. He's 30 years old and still likely has several quality seasons left under his belt. The Cardinals aren't going to contend for the postseason, and Baker is their best asset for future value.  
Josh Sweat is having a down year, both sack-wise (2 in 7 games) and in terms of his pressure rate (7.9%). And his contract doesn't exactly make that type of production attractive. But his track record over the long term, up to and including last year, is much more impressive, and teams could bet that he has a bounce-back in a more favorable environment. He probably wants a new contract, but that could be worked out once you see him play for your team. Jacoby Brissett is clearly not the long-term answer under center for the Cardinals, and they might turn to Carson Beck sooner rather than later so they can see what they have in the third-round pick before making a decision on whether to select a quarterback in next year's draft. That makes Brissett expendable, and some team looking for a quality backup or fill-in for an injured starter could be interested in his services. The Dolphins 
Win over the Jets notwithstanding, the Dolphins look like arguably the worst team in the league this season. Zach Sieler, though, remains a quality player. He hasn't been at his best this season (nobody on the Dolphins has), but we've seen high upside as both a run defender and a pass rusher from the defensive interior. If you can tap back into that, his base salaries over the next few years are very affordable ($44.5 million from 2027 through 2029, none of which is guaranteed). 
Jordyn Brooks, like Jeffery Simmons and Derwin James, recently signed an extension. But his deal actually made him easier to trade and gave the Dolphins the benefit of selling to an acquiring team, knowing they'd have Brooks under team control for multiple years. With the emergence of rookie Jacob Rodriguez and Brooks having recently turned 29 years old, they could look to deal him for a pretty sizable return. Brian Thomas Jr.  
Brian Thomas Jr. has pretty clearly fallen out of favor in Jacksonville. In the Jaguars' last game, he didn't play a single second-half snap. Rookie Josh Cameron is playing ahead of him, and now it seems that two-way star Travis Hunter might be as well. But Thomas has more of a track record of high-level production than did Marvin Harrison Jr., and MHJ fetched a second-round pick via trade. If the Jaguars could get that type of return, they should be very interested, and teams should be interested in acquiring him as well, considering what he did as a rookie (albeit maybe not for quite that high a price, considering what he's done this year and last).Daron Payne 
The Commanders are going nowhere and Daron Payne is in the final year of his contract. His $16.4 million base salary is high but not prohibitive to a trade. He's still a quality run defender, even if he doesn't give you that much in the way of pass-rush juice these days. The Commies would be wise to get something for him before he leaves in free agency next offseason. 
Will McDonald IV 
Will McDonald IV has seen his snap rate cut from 66% down to 46% this season after the arrival of David Bailey in the draft. But he had 10.5 and 8 sacks over the last two seasons, and has shown he can be a productive pass rusher. The Jets just lost to the aforementioned Dolphins, so it's not like they're really going to compete for anything this year. McDonald had his fifth-year option picked up for next season, but he's still affordable. Kirk Cousins 
Klint Kubiak is already getting questions about when he's going to turn the reins over to Fernando Mendoza, which means Kirk Cousins' time under center is likely coming to an end fairly soon. Like Brissett, he could be valuable to a team looking for either a quality backup or a fill-in starter for the rest of the season. The Raiders might prefer to just keep him around and have him mentor Mendoza for the rest of the year, though. Jauan Jennings
Jauan Jennings has so far been entirely uninvolved in the Vikings' offense. It would be surprising to see the league's last remanining unbeaten team make a trade where the give away an asset instead of acquire one, but given Jennings' lack of role and the number of teams in need of wide receiver help, this is certainly a situation worth monitoring.

title: Davion Mitchell lays out problem of Bam Adebayo's fit with Giannis Antetokounmpo - CBS Sports

body:
It's been a struggle for Adebayo to find space to operate next to Antetokounmpo as Miami is off to an 0-4 start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Miami Heat are off to a dreadful start to the 2026-27 season, dropping their first four games after a 113-109 loss on Monday night to the Dallas Mavericks. It's not the start anyone in Miami envisioned after trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo this summer, and all of the worst fears about the Heat's roster and a potentially clunky offensive fit between Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have already come to fruition in the first week of the season. Adebayo is off to the worst start to a season in his career since becoming a full-time starter, averaging 11.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game on 40.0/16.7/61.5 shooting splits -- all of which would represent career-low shooting marks. A four-game sample is not enough to entirely write off the partnership, but it has been about the worst-case scenario for how those two stars can work off of each other. Adebayo said outside critics are making him out to be "the scapegoat" of Miami's early-season struggles, but with a roster already thin on offensive talent, the Heat's second star struggling this badly is going to bring quite the spotlight. 

        
            
                Winners and losers of NBA's first week: Giannis' Heat are ice cold, OKC injuries and new-look wonders
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Davion Mitchell, the team's starting point guard, was asked about Adebayo's struggles after Monday's loss to Dallas and succinctly explained why it's a tough fit alongside Antetokounmpo. "I think I got to do a better job of not letting [Adebayo] get lost in the game," Mitchell said, via ESPN. "He got to be more aggressive. I think that he will. He's still trying to figure it out because I said this before -- I think him and Giannis play in the same spaces, and then when Giannis is on the floor, he's on the floor. He can't be in those spaces, and but it's something to get used to."That was always the concern with that partnership, and as Mitchell noted, if it's a matter of Adebayo or Antetokounmpo being in his preferred spot, it's almost always going to be Antetokounmpo getting his way. The problem is that it puts Adebayo in spots where he's uncomfortable. And even when he is getting touches in his best spots, the spacing is off because Antetokounmpo also wants to get to the paint. 
Perhaps the most worrisome part of this for Adebayo is that Antetokounmpo's history tells us he's not going to change for the betterment of his co-star. Antetokounmpo's partnership with Damian Lillard made it abundantly clear that he's not the type to adjust his game tremendously to make for a better fit with a star, as he didn't want to be part of a pick-and-roll-heavy two-man game with Lillard that could've made the Bucks' offense special. That means there's little reason to expect Antetokounmpo to suddenly recognize he and Adebayo want to play in similar spots and to yield that position to Adebayo more often. If that's the case, the onus gets put on Adebayo to completely alter his game 10 years into his NBA career. So far, that reinvention isn't going very well, as his 3-point shot has not fallen and he's struggling to get opportunities inside -- his 6.8 2-point attempts per game are by far his lowest since becoming a starter in his third season. 
As Mitchell notes, some of it comes down to Adebayo being more aggressive, but it's harder to do so when you aren't in comfortable spots. With Antetokounmpo unlikely to change his style to help Adebayo adapt, it's going to be up to Adebayo to sink or swim in this new partnership.

        Utah Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. suffered a torn MCL in his right knee on Monday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, the team announced Tuesday. Jackson's injury, which came in the first quarter of Monday's loss to the Memphis Grizzlies when Ty Jerome fell into his knee, will not require surgery, according to ESPN.That wasn't the only front-court injury Utah sustained in the loss, as Lauri Markkanen injured his wrist attempting to get around a screen in the first quarter. The team said Tuesday that Markkanen is considered day-to-day. Neither returned to the game as they played just 16 combined minutes in the defeat.Even if Markkanen avoids serious injury, Jackson's absence puts the Jazz in an enormously difficult situation, considering the direction their offseason took. After a contract standoff with former starting center Walker Kessler, the Jazz elected to sign-and-trade him to the Los Angeles Lakers for two first-round picks and two first-round swaps. It's early, but Kessler has been spectacular for the Lakers, and his absence left the Jazz without a long-term option at center. Short-term starter Jusuf Nurkić is also injured, and now, the Jazz are without Jackson, their rim-protecting power forward.
Utah has spent the bulk of the past four seasons tanking. This season carried at least Play-In expectations after the emergence of Keyonte George last year and with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson. Those goals are obviously not out of reach even with Jackson injured, but a 1-3 start coupled with everything they've lost in the front-court certainly leaves Utah behind the eight ball early on. The Jazz already rank No. 25 in the NBA defensively, and while their rebounding has surprised early in the season, it is a clear weakness on paper.The Jazz have the ammunition to make a sizable trade if they want to. That was one of the benefits of trading Kessler. But teams are rarely eager to give away valuable veterans early in seasons, and roughly 29% of all NBA players are not currently eligible for trades because of contracts they signed during the offseason. 
For now, Utah will probably have to rely on incumbent big men like Jaxson Hayes, Mo Bamba and Kyle Filipowski while they await the return of at least Nurkić and then, eventually, Jackson.
